editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Previously on Elsewhere

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Five years ago, a Directorate operation ended in a warehouse fire. Six people died, including Elise Varen, Ninja's older sister. Hex, an operative sent to recover a stolen archive, disobeyed orders and tried to save the people trapped inside. He escaped with Elise's damaged phone and a photograph of Ninja, then vanished under the name Elias Ward.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja was told the fire was an accident. She spent years grieving Elise and fighting strange accusations attached to her employment records. Hex hid in the mountain village of Bellwether, repairing machinery for an older man named Tomas. Only recently did he discover that the woman in his photograph was Elise's sister.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: And now, without knowing any of that, Ninja has arrived in Bellwether for a few days away.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Chapter One — The Room Above the Bakery

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The first thing Ninja learned about Bellwether was that the village had a personal disagreement with straightforward roads.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The second was that nobody appeared particularly interested in resolving it.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She passed the same stone fountain twice before deciding the road signs were either decorative or malicious.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Excellent,

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: she told the dashboard.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: I've been here twelve minutes and the village is already bullying me.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Rain stippled the windscreen. Beyond the narrow lane, cottages leaned together beneath slate roofs. Window boxes spilled stubborn late-season flowers over old stone walls, and somewhere a church bell rang five times with the weary confidence of something that had never once been late.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Her accommodation was called Briar House. The booking photograph had shown a charming doorway beneath ivy.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The actual doorway was charming, certainly. It was also hidden down an alley barely wider than her luggage.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She parked where a handwritten sign instructed VISITORS, PLEASE DON'T BLOCK THE MILK VAN, and dragged her bag across the wet cobbles.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: At the door, a small brass bell hung beneath a sign: RING ONCE. WE HEARD YOU.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja rang once.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: A moment later she heard footsteps, the scrape of a bolt, and a woman calling, “Coming! Unless you're selling windows, in which case I've died!”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The door opened on a woman in her sixties wearing a wool cardigan and the expression of someone who had already formed an opinion.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “You're the booking.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: I am,

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja said.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Although I did consider becoming a permanent resident of the roundabout.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Ah. The fountain?”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Twice.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Only twice? You're practically local.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The woman introduced herself as Ada, owner of Briar House, occasional baker, and apparently unofficial keeper of the village's entire social history.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She led Ninja upstairs past framed landscape photographs and a staircase that complained beneath every step.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Breakfast is downstairs at eight,” Ada said. “Unless you sleep in. Then it's at nine. Unless I sleep in, in which case we negotiate.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Sounds fair. Although I should warn you, I'm very competitive at sleeping in.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Then you've come to the right establishment,” Ada said. “I haven't lost a morning yet.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “There's hot water, mostly. The radiator knocks when the wind changes. That's normal.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Is there anything that isn't normal?

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ada considered.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “The mayor's brother.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja laughed before she could stop herself.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Her room was small and warm, with a brass bed, a thick quilt, a writing desk, and a window looking across rooftops toward the mountains. A kettle sat beside two mismatched cups. Someone had left a sprig of rosemary in a narrow vase.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: For a moment, standing there with her suitcase still in her hand, Ninja felt the peculiar loneliness of arriving somewhere nobody expected anything from her.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: No work calls. No letters demanding explanations. No one asking whether she'd heard anything more about the investigation.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She could be a stranger for a few days.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ada put the room key on the desk.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “There's a map downstairs. Don't trust it too much. They changed the bridge footpath three years ago and nobody's told the printer.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Of course they haven't.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “And if you get hungry, The Crooked Lantern serves supper. Tell Maeve I sent you.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Will that get me a discount?

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Absolutely not. But she'll know you're not a menace.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja raised an eyebrow.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ada looked at her pink hair and dark coat, then smiled.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Well. Not a dangerous one, anyway.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: After the door closed, Ninja sat on the edge of the bed and listened to the rain. She took out her phone, opened her messages, and stopped at Elise's name.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She hadn't meant to.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Her thumb hovered over the conversation. For a second she imagined sending a picture of the room, followed by a complaint about the staircase.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Elise would have replied that the house was haunted, and that Ninja should befriend the ghost because it probably had better directions.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja smiled at the thought.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Then she placed the phone face down.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Okay,

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: she whispered to the quiet room.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: I'm here.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Outside, the mountains disappeared behind a low band of cloud.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Chapter Two — A Village with Opinions

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: An hour later, the rain had softened into mist.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja pulled on her coat and went exploring with a vague plan involving coffee, a walk, and not accidentally joining a local committee.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Bellwether's main street curved around the fountain, then divided into three lanes that seemed to have been designed by people who disliked one another.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: There was a grocery shop with crates of apples outside, a tiny bookshop whose window displayed more handwritten notes than books, and a florist with a sleepy dog sprawled across the entrance.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja crouched beside the dog.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Hello, gorgeous. Are you employed here?
editorialCues.attempt: Recorded attempt reported; no recoverable audio verified. Recover the original if possible, otherwise record this exact text.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The dog opened one eye, decided she was acceptable, and returned to sleep.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: A voice from inside the shop said, “That's Inspector.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Inspector?
editorialCues.attempt: Recorded attempt reported; no recoverable audio verified. Recover the original if possible, otherwise record this exact text.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “He supervises everyone. Doesn't do any work.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Management material,
editorialCues.attempt: Recorded attempt reported; no recoverable audio verified. Recover the original if possible, otherwise record this exact text.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja said.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: No meetings, no emails, and he gets to nap in the doorway. Honestly, I'd like to apply.
editorialCues.attempt: Recorded attempt reported; no recoverable audio verified. Recover the original if possible, otherwise record this exact text.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The florist laughed.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Does he accept bribes?
editorialCues.attempt: Recorded attempt reported; no recoverable audio verified. Recover the original if possible, otherwise record this exact text.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja asked.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Only biscuits.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Finally. A reasonable boss.
editorialCues.attempt: Recorded attempt reported; no recoverable audio verified. Recover the original if possible, otherwise record this exact text.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: At the bookshop, she bought a second-hand paperback because the cover featured a dramatic woman running across a moor in a dress wholly unsuitable for running across a moor.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The bookseller, a narrow man with round spectacles, studied her purchase.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “That one's terrible.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Excellent recommendation.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “The ending makes no sense.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Now I absolutely have to read it. If the ending is terrible, I'm coming back to complain.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “People usually do.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Good. I'll bring a detailed report. Possibly diagrams.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He wrapped it in brown paper and pointed her toward a café beside the old bridge.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The café was called The Narrow Cup. Its owner had filled the windows with plants and apparently surrendered the remaining space to mismatched furniture.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja ordered coffee and a cinnamon bun large enough to constitute a legal threat.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She took a table beside the window.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Across the street, two older men argued over whether the village clock was seven minutes fast or eight minutes slow. Neither appeared to consider the possibility that both were wrong.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She watched a woman cross the square carrying a violin case and a bag of potatoes. A delivery driver reversed three times to avoid a cat that was clearly enjoying the power.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: It was all gloriously ordinary.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: And ordinary, Ninja discovered, could feel unfamiliar when you'd spent years waiting for the next terrible letter.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She opened her paperback and read three pages before realising she had been staring at the same sentence.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Her phone buzzed with a work-related notification.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Her stomach tightened on instinct.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She checked it. Nothing urgent. A routine reminder she could deal with after the trip.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Still, the familiar pressure remained behind her ribs, as though the world had reached across the mountains to remind her that peace came with conditions.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja set the phone down.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The café owner appeared beside her table with a small glass of water.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “First day here?” the woman asked.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Is it that obvious?

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “You're looking at the square like it's a television programme.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: It's a pretty good one. The cat's my favourite character. He has the confidence of someone who's never paid rent in his life.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “That's Mayor. Not officially. He just believes it.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja laughed.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The woman nodded toward the window.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Walk up to the old overlook before sunset. Best view in the village. Unless the clouds are in a mood.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Are they usually?

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Constantly.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja thanked her, finished her coffee, and tucked the paperback under her arm.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: As she left, she realised she hadn't thought about the warehouse for nearly twenty minutes.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The realisation hurt a little.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Then she let herself be pleased anyway.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Chapter Three — The Workshop at the Edge of Town

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: At the forestry workshop, Hex was trying to convince a stubborn engine that their disagreement did not need to become personal.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The engine disagreed.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He leaned over the open bonnet, sleeves rolled to his elbows, dark hair tied back loosely enough that strands kept escaping around his face.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Come on,” he muttered.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Behind him, Tomas made a thoughtful noise.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Have you tried being polite?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “I've tried everything else.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Could threaten to replace it.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “That's your management philosophy?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Worked on you.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex turned his head.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas grinned over the rim of his mug.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: They'd spent the morning repairing a vehicle belonging to a forestry crew. The owner had described the problem as a little rattle, which had turned out to mean a fractured bracket, two loose belts, and a noise resembling a cupboard full of angry cutlery.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex tightened the final fitting and stepped back.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Try it.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas turned the key.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The engine started cleanly.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “See?” Tomas said. “Politeness.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex wiped his hands on a rag. “You should write a manual.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “People would buy it.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Only to use as firewood.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The workshop telephone rang.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas answered, listened, and made the weary expression he reserved for requests that began with just a quick favour.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Yes, Maeve. Yes, I remember. No, I haven't forgotten.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex looked up.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas covered the receiver.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “The Lantern's kitchen extractor is making that noise again.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Which noise?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “The one that apparently sounds like a ghost swallowing cutlery.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Helpful diagnosis.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas returned to the call. “He'll take a look after closing.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex stared at him.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas smiled innocently.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: When the call ended, Hex said, “I don't recall volunteering.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “You were about to.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Was I?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Eventually. Once you finished pretending you weren't.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex shook his head, but he didn't argue.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The Crooked Lantern was one of the few places in Bellwether he visited without automatically planning an exit. Maeve, its owner, had long ago decided that Elias Ward was quiet rather than unfriendly. She kept his preferred table near the side wall and never asked questions about his past.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: That suited him.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Still, the message from the encrypted channel sat folded in his coat pocket.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Relationship to deceased courier: sibling.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He had read it so many times the words seemed engraved on the back of his eyes.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He thought about the photograph beneath his floorboard. The woman smiling outside a café. He had kept it because throwing it away felt wrong, and looking at it felt worse.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas set down his mug.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “You're miles away again.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Thinking.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Dangerous habit.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex tried a smile.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas watched him for a moment, then said, more quietly, “Whatever's going on, don't spend the whole evening alone with it.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex looked at the open workshop door, where the mist drifted through the yard.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “I have to fix Maeve's extractor, remember?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “That's a start.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Chapter Four — The Overlook

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The path to the old overlook began behind the church and climbed through a stand of beech trees.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja followed the signs until the signs stopped, which felt entirely consistent with everything else she'd learned about Bellwether.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The path was muddy but manageable. Wet leaves shone beneath her boots, and the air smelled of earth, rain, and woodsmoke carried up from the village.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Halfway up, she stopped to catch her breath.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Not because the hill was especially steep, she told herself, but because the trees were very interesting and deserved her full attention.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: A robin landed on a fence post a few feet away.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Don't judge me,

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: she told it.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The robin offered no reassurance.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: At the top, a low stone wall marked the edge of the overlook. Beyond it, Bellwether spread across the valley like a handful of houses carefully placed between the hills. Smoke curled from chimneys. The narrow bridge crossed a stream that glittered through the trees. Farther away, the mountains rose in overlapping shades of blue-grey.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja leaned against the wall.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: For the first time since arriving, she was completely still.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She took a photograph, then another, trying to capture the way the clouds opened briefly over the distant ridge.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She wished Elise could see it.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The thought came without warning, but not with the sharpness it once had. More like a hand resting gently on an old bruise.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Elise,

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: she said under her breath,

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: you would have complained about the walk all the way up.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She rested her elbows on the cold stone.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Actually, you'd have made me carry your bag. Then you'd tell everyone you practically dragged me to the summit.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Her smile wavered.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: I wish I could show you this. I wish I could tell you about the ridiculous cat and the woman who runs the guesthouse like a tiny dictatorship.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: And Elise would have done it theatrically, stopping every fifty steps to announce that her younger sister was trying to murder her for the sake of a photograph.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja laughed softly.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She imagined the two of them standing there, Elise pretending not to be impressed.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The empty space beside her remained empty.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: But the view was still beautiful.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: After a while, Ninja took her phone out and opened the saved voice message.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hello, menace. I'm outside your building. I have food.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She listened only once.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Then she slipped the phone into her pocket, pulled her coat tighter, and watched the last sunlight move across the rooftops.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: A small part of her had been afraid that enjoying the trip would mean leaving Elise behind.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Standing there, she understood something different.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Elise had loved her. She would have wanted her to go places, eat enormous cinnamon buns, get lost in ridiculous villages, and have stories to tell.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja brushed moisture from her cheek before deciding whether it was rain.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Fine,

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: she murmured.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: You win. I'm having a holiday.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She looked down at the village lights.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: And yes, I'm going to eat another cinnamon bun tomorrow. Don't start.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Below her, the lights of The Crooked Lantern flickered on.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Chapter Five — Supper at the Lantern

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The Crooked Lantern looked as though someone had built a pub, discovered halfway through that straight lines were optional, and committed to the decision.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Its sign swung above a narrow doorway. Warm light spilled onto the cobbles. Through the windows Ninja could see a low ceiling crossed by dark beams and people sitting close around wooden tables.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She stood outside for a moment.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Going into an unfamiliar pub alone was not a tragedy. She knew that.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Her brain, however, had prepared a brief but passionate argument against it.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She ignored the argument and opened the door.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Warmth met her first. Then the smell of roasted potatoes, old wood, and something simmering with enough garlic to make its presence known from across the room.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Conversation dipped briefly as she entered, not out of hostility but because Bellwether appeared to notice everything.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: A woman behind the bar looked up.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Evening. You must be staying with Ada.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja stopped.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Is there a village-wide announcement system? Because if there is, I'd like to request that my getting lost remain classified.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Only Ada.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Terrifying.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “I'm Maeve.” The woman smiled. “Find a seat. Kitchen's still open.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja chose a small table beside a bookshelf filled with abandoned paperbacks and board games missing their instructions.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: A chalkboard listed the evening's food in handwriting that became progressively less patient toward the bottom.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She ordered stew and bread.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: While she waited, she watched the room.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Two men played cards beneath a crooked photograph of the village in winter. A young couple shared chips near the fireplace. At the bar, a man in a green jacket told a story so elaborate that even the people who'd clearly heard it before leaned in for the ending.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja found herself smiling.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve brought the stew in a heavy ceramic bowl.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “First time in Bellwether?”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Yes.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Good choice?”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Ask me after I've survived the roads. At this point I'm convinced the fountain moves when nobody's looking.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Ah. The fountain.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Does everyone know about the fountain?

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Everyone who's ever arrived here.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The stew was excellent. Ninja ate slowly, listening to the crackle of the fire and the soft, overlapping conversations.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: At one point, a little girl at a nearby table dropped a wooden toy beneath Ninja's chair.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja retrieved it and handed it back.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Your dragon escaped. Should I be worried about the village, or is he one of the friendly ones?

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “He does that,” the girl said gravely.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Sounds like a troublemaker.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “He's a very good dragon.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Of course. My mistake. I'll make sure to address him as Your Majesty next time.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The girl's father thanked her, and the child spent the next five minutes explaining, with extraordinary seriousness, the dragon's entire family history.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja listened as though receiving a classified briefing.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: It felt good to be useful in a way that didn't demand anything from her.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: When the family left, she ordered tea.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The pub had grown busier. Rain tapped the windows again, gentle at first and then harder.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve glanced toward the door.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Elias is late.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Who's Elias?” asked one of the card players.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “The only person in this village who can persuade that extractor to behave.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Have you tried asking it nicely?” someone called.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve rolled her eyes.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja looked up from her cup only because the name was unfamiliar. It meant nothing to her.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Not yet.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Chapter Six — The Man Who Almost Stayed Home

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Across the village, Hex stood in his rented kitchen staring at the tin box on the table.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He had taken it from beneath the floorboard without entirely deciding why.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Inside lay the photograph, its corners softened from years of handling, and Elise's damaged phone, long dead.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He hadn't looked at either for weeks.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tonight he picked up the photograph.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja was laughing at something outside the frame. Whoever had taken the picture had caught her in an unguarded moment, head turned slightly, expression alive with mischief.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He wondered what she sounded like.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The question startled him.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: For five years he had thought of her as a responsibility, a consequence, a person he had failed without ever meeting. It was easier to think in those terms than to imagine the life she actually lived.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He set the photograph down.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Mara's voice came back to him from the motel years ago.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Walk away from this. You can still have a life.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He had walked away, but the life he'd built was made of careful absences. No photographs on the walls. No old friends. No questions he couldn't answer.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas was the closest thing he had to family now, though neither of them had ever said so.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex folded the report and returned it to the tin.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Then he put on his coat.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The extractor at The Crooked Lantern needed fixing.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: That was a normal problem. A solvable problem. Something that would not require him to decide whether he owed a stranger the truth about her sister's death.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He locked the door and headed into the rain.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Halfway down the street, his phone vibrated.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: An unknown number.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He stopped beneath the awning of the closed grocer's shop.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The screen displayed a single message.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: YOU SHOULD HAVE STAYED GONE.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex read it twice.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: No sender. No explanation.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The rain sounded suddenly louder.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He checked the street behind him.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Empty, except for the reflected glow of the lamps in puddles.
editorialCues.note: If Part 3 says ‘lamps and puddles’, record this exact sentence with Wade.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: It might have been a cruel joke. A wrong number. Someone who had found an old contact.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He knew better than to believe that without evidence.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He deleted the message, then regretted deleting it.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: For a moment he considered going home.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Instead he looked toward the pub, where warm light showed through the rain.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He had spent five years letting the Directorate decide how much of his life he was allowed to have.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Not tonight,” he said quietly.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: And he kept walking.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Chapter Seven — The Crooked Door

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Inside the pub, Ninja had reached the point where she was contemplating a second dessert despite being completely full.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The little girl with the toy dragon had left behind a paper napkin covered in drawings. Maeve picked it up and showed Ninja.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Apparently you've been appointed guardian of the dragon.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja studied the scribbles.

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: That's a serious responsibility. Does it come with a salary, or am I being paid entirely in dragon drawings?

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “I'll have to warn Ada.”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Please don't. She already thinks I'm a menace. I'd like to maintain at least twenty-four hours of plausible innocence.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve laughed and returned to the bar.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: A gust of cold air pushed through the room as the door opened.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja didn't turn immediately. She was busy trying to work out whether the dessert menu's promise of a modest portion was legally enforceable.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Across the threshold stepped a tall man in a dark coat, rain glistening in his long hair. He paused just inside to shake water from his sleeves.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve looked up.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Elias! I was about to send a search party.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Would you have paid them?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Absolutely not.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Then I'm surprised anyone volunteers.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He spoke quietly, with the dry amusement of someone who preferred to let other people do most of the talking.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja glanced toward the bar.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She saw his profile first: the dark beard, the tired eyes, the line of an eyebrow piercing catching the lamplight. Tattoos disappeared beneath his collar.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He was speaking to Maeve, not looking around the room.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: There was nothing dramatic about it.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: No thunderclap. No sudden silence. No sense that the universe had rearranged itself.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Just a stranger arriving at a pub on a rainy evening.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja looked back at her menu.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Across the room, Hex accepted a toolbox from Maeve and headed toward the narrow passage beside the kitchen.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He never saw Ninja's face.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Not yet.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The extractor gave a mournful metallic screech.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: From the passage, Hex called, “Is that the ghost?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve shouted back, “That's the ghost.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja laughed into her tea.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: A few minutes later, the noise stopped.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The room applauded.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex reappeared, wiping his hands with a cloth, looking faintly embarrassed by the attention.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas, who had arrived while he was working, raised his glass.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Our village hero.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “It's a fan belt, Tomas.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “A modest hero.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex shook his head and took the seat Maeve indicated at the far end of the bar.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He was tired. The strange message still sat in the back of his mind. He told himself he would stay for one drink and leave.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja finished her tea and stood to pay.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: At the bar, Maeve was helping another customer. Ninja waited, looking at the photographs behind the bottles.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: One showed Bellwether beneath deep snow. Another showed a younger Tomas standing beside a tractor with a triumphant expression.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She heard a man beside her say, “You should charge more for the extractor repairs.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve answered, “And ruin my reputation for taking advantage of you?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja smiled at the exchange.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex was standing a few steps away, reaching for his coat.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: For one small moment they occupied the same patch of warm light, separated by a stool, a stack of clean glasses, and the fact that neither had looked directly at the other.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve took Ninja's payment.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Did you enjoy the stew?”

editorialCues.speaker: ninja
editorialCues.text: Very much. I might come back tomorrow.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Do. We need someone who appreciates the food without giving me an engineering report.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: From behind her, Hex said, “The engineering reports are complimentary.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja laughed and turned halfway toward the voice.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: But at that exact moment, the front door opened and a cluster of wet hikers came in, blocking the space between them.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Someone called for Maeve. Tomas asked Hex a question. Ninja stepped aside to let the hikers through.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: The moment passed.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She pulled up her hood and left.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Outside, the rain had become a fine silver mist.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Ninja walked back toward Briar House with the smell of woodsmoke in her coat and the pleasant ache of a day spent doing things she hadn't needed to do.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: She was thinking about the cinnamon bun, the ridiculous book, and whether the dog named Inspector might permit another visit tomorrow.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Inside the pub, Hex sat down again.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve set a glass in front of him.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “New guest at Ada's,” she said casually. “Seems nice.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Good for Ada.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Pink hair. Funny. Got lost at the fountain twice.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex's hand stopped against the glass.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He looked toward the door.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Pink hair?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Maeve was already moving away.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “Bright pink. Can't miss her.”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex stood.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas looked up. “Where are you going?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex didn't answer immediately.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Outside the window, a hooded figure turned the corner and disappeared into the mist.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He hadn't seen her face. He had no reason to believe that every woman with pink hair was the one in the photograph.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: But his heart was beating too fast.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: He sat back down, slowly.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Tomas watched him with a troubled expression.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “You all right?”

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Hex stared at the doorway.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: “No,” he said.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: And this time, he didn't pretend otherwise.

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: End of Episode Two

editorialCues.speaker: wade
editorialCues.text: Next time on Elsewhere: The Stranger at the Bar. A second evening at The Crooked Lantern finally brings Ninja and Elias face to face. One of them thinks it's a chance meeting. The other knows a photograph, a dead sister, and five years of secrets are standing between them.
